text: Track 5.2 And this is the space for our new leisure centre. What do you think Jenny? It's an amazing space with great potential. I can't believe how much has happened since I've been away. I've got a million questions. Are the architects working on the planning yet? Yes, we have two firms working on different aspects of the project now. One is focusing on giving the internal spaces a new lease of life, the other on the outside landscaping. Here, let me show you how the internal plan is looking. Great! What are you doing with this space on the plan here? Maybe we could have an open plan design. Quite a bit. As you can see, it's more like a prison than an office in its current form. We need to open it up so we can create more light. Look at these internal walls. We intend to knock them down as they are about to collapse and we are also going to raise the roof in the far right corner so that we can introduce a large skylight. This will allow both light and fresh air into the space. Wow! It's ambitious, isn't it? If I've understood correctly, this is a conservation area so the designs need to be sustainable. There are rules and regulations we'll need to follow and that takes time. We won't be able to cut corners when it comes to the design in order to get things done quicker. You're right. Well, both architects we are using specializing sustainable construction and we have instructed them that we want to achieve a development that is sympathetic to the existing area. They're not cheap, of course. But they are experts in their field and once the development is complete, it'll be a potential gold mine attracting both local and national businesses to the area. Let's take a look outside. Wow! What a beautiful setting! The last time I was here it was an absolute mess but now the land's been cleared, we can really see how it might be transformed. That lake there and the way the land slopes towards those trees is stunning. I really think we should have a restaurant with an outdoor terrace on the water's edge. It would be a fantastic addition. That was our intention, but since you've been away, things have got a bit controversial. I was told by senior management that the lake is in fact the habitat for a rare species of frog. Oh, I see. I'm guessing there are serious challenges to overcome. Yes, there are a few. Firstly, we won't be able to obtain permission to build within 100 meters of the frog's habitat which means we need to think about other options. It's going to be extremely challenging for me to get the existing plans revised within the time scale we have in mind. That's terrible! You must be concerned after all your hard work. I know you had high hopes for that area in particular and time is money, isn't it? Any delay is going to mean that we will lose potential profits. Absolutely, but we must take care of the wildlife. So, although changing the design is controversial and we may lose money, we need to get back to the drawing board on this part of the project. We will have to think again about the lakeside development completely. Wouldn't it be better if we turned the lake into a wildlife conservation area? Not only could we protect the frog's habitat, but we could also encourage species of birds and insects into the area. That could be an excellent feature for bringing tourists to the development. That is exactly what I was thinking, Jenny. And let's discuss it a bit further.
